summary: Round r1 (restricted network; data hosts blocked; one web search used). The research question (which use of a marginal GWh - export or domestic industry - yields more national value added) is PENDING: no price, tariff, cost or value-added parameter was retrieved. Designed: a seasonal opportunity-cost table in NPR_per_MWh that classifies each Nepali month (and, where needed, time block) into three regimes - wet-season spill (export limit binding: opportunity cost zero), export-marginal (opportunity cost = realised export netback), and dry-season import-marginal (opportunity cost = landed import cost). The domestic column is industrial value added per GWh net of annualised capital cost of new industry, plus the tariff paid to the utility, minus incremental grid cost and losses, consistent with energy.MarginalUseComparison. Export value uses NEA realised border netback by route (per 22B), with IEX prices as upper reference; INR converted at the NRB NPR/INR peg rate for the same month. Leads: ERC tariff order (located by search), NEA annual/system reports, IEX and CERC price data, CERC cross-border regulations, CEA approval pages, NRB exchange rates, NSO Census of Manufacturing Establishments.

findings.claim: Realised export netback per MWh at the Nepal border, by market route (IEX exchange sale via NVVN, bilateral, Nepal-Bangladesh trilateral) and by Nepali month / season.
findings.note: Compute from NEA annual report export revenue (NPR) / export energy (kWh converted to MWh) by route and month; cross-check against CERC cross-border section. Per 22B challenge, this (not the IEX clearing price) is the export value.

findings.claim: IEX DAM / G-DAM / RTM clearing prices by Nepali month and wet/dry season (upper reference for export value) in INR per MWh.
findings.note: Taken from 22B regional_price_profile once retrieved; not re-derived here. Indian FY and calendar months re-aggregated to Nepali months.

findings.claim: Deductions from exchange price to Nepal-border netback: exchange transaction fee, NVVN trading margin, Indian transmission charges and losses applicable to cross-border schedules, Nepal-side wheeling to the border point, deviation-settlement exposure.
findings.note: From CERC CBTE Regulations 2019 and amendments, NVVN terms and NEA accounts; each component recorded separately with its regulatory vintage.

findings.claim: Import landed cost per MWh from India in dry-season months (exchange price plus charges, and bilateral/G2G contract prices), by month.
findings.note: From NEA annual report import cost (NPR) / import energy by route and month; HP-DAM as evening-peak ceiling reference. This is the opportunity cost of an extra domestic GWh in import-marginal months.

findings.claim: Industrial consumer tariff: energy charge and demand charge by supply voltage (LV/MV/HV), with any time-of-day or seasonal differentiation, and the realised average industrial tariff (industrial revenue / industrial GWh).
findings.note: ERC tariff order (vintage to verify) for the schedule; NEA annual report for realised average. Demand charges are converted to per-MWh only with a stated load factor (assumption A4), reported separately from energy charges.
findings.period: tariff order in force FY2082/83 (2025/26) and FY2083/84 (2026/27); realised FY2021/22-FY2025/26

findings.claim: Incremental grid cost and technical loss factor for delivering one additional MWh to an industrial consumer (distribution/sub-transmission cost, losses at MV/HV, reliability cost of dedicated feeders).
findings.note: NEA distribution loss by voltage/centre and cost-of-service data; ERC tariff-order cost-of-service annexes if published. Losses enter as a gross-up of energy required at the busbar, not as a price.

findings.claim: Manufacturing value added per GWh of electricity consumed, by ISIC 2-digit industry (average ratio), current prices.
findings.note: Census of Manufacturing Establishments: VA / electricity consumed (kWh -> GWh); electricity expenditure / kWh as a check on the tariff actually paid. Average VA/GWh is NOT the marginal VA attributable to electricity (see caveats).
findings.period: latest census round (Nepal FY label to record)

findings.claim: Capital cost and annualised capital charge per GWh/year of new electricity-intensive industrial capacity (cement, steel re-rolling/ferro-alloys, data centres, electrolytic hydrogen/ammonia), and its utilisation in dry season.
findings.note: No Nepal-specific primary source located in r1. Requires project appraisal documents (IBN/DoInd approvals), or international cost references (IEA) with an explicit transfer assumption; coordinate with 05B and 24B.

findings.claim: Hours/months in which the cross-border transfer limit or CEA-approved quantum binds in the wet season, and the energy spilled (GWh) as a result.
findings.note: From NEA system-operation reports and 05A seasonal_profile / transmission_bottlenecks; CEA approval orders for approved MW. Determines whether the marginal wet-season GWh has export value or zero value (spill).

findings.claim: NPR/INR conversion rate (peg) and NPR/USD rate for each period used.
findings.note: NRB daily reference rates via forex page / API; use the middle of buying and selling rates, averaged over the same months as the price data; regime statement from NRB monetary policy.

findings.claim: The comparison is made per marginal MWh delivered at the generator busbar in Nepal; the generation cost of that MWh is the same under both uses and cancels out, so it is excluded from both columns.

Seasons follow the NEA hydrological calendar on Nepali months as agreed by 05A/22B (wet = Jestha-Kartik, dry = remaining months); each month is additionally classified into a regime: spill (export constrained), export-marginal, or import-marginal.

INR amounts are converted to NPR at the NRB reference rate for the same month (middle rate); USD comparisons use NRB NPR/USD for the same month. No annual-to-annual conversion across fiscal and calendar years.
Demand charges are converted to an equivalent per-MWh charge only through an explicitly stated industrial load factor, reported as a sensitivity range, never a single default.
The domestic column is evaluated for new (incremental) industrial demand; existing industry's use is already in the baseline and is not re-valued.

data_gaps: All parameters of the table (export netback, import cost, industrial tariff, grid cost, loss factor, VA/GWh, capital charge, export limit, exchange rates) - no document downloaded in r1.
ERC tariff order vintage: the order located by search is labelled 2078; the order in force for FY2082/83 and FY2083/84 must be confirmed from erc.gov.np.
NVVN trading margin and exact Indian transmission charges/losses for Nepal cross-border schedules - regulatory text located, applied values not.
Capital cost of new electricity-intensive industry in Nepal: no primary source located; needs IBN/DoInd project documents or an explicitly labelled international reference (with 05B, 24B).
Marginal (as opposed to average) value added attributable to electricity: no Nepal study located; method relies on bounds.
Block-level (hourly/15-minute) Nepal export/import schedules needed for the dry-season off-peak regime; NEA monthly data may be insufficient.
Spill (energy not evacuated) records by month - availability in NEA publications unconfirmed (shared gap with 05A).
WECS and NVVN are not in the source catalog (proposed to 00A).

assumptions.text: Comparison per marginal MWh at the Nepal generator busbar; generation cost identical under both uses and excluded.
Seasons on NEA hydrological calendar in Nepali months (wet = Jestha-Kartik), each month classified as spill, export-marginal or import-marginal.
INR -> NPR at NRB middle reference rate for the same month; no cross fiscal/calendar-year annual conversion.
Demand charges converted to per-MWh only via a stated load-factor range.
Domestic column evaluates new incremental industrial demand only.

challenges.text: energy.MarginalUseComparison lacks (i) a seasonal regime (spill / export-marginal / import-marginal) with import landed cost as the dry-season opportunity cost, (ii) a loss factor, and (iii) a capital-charge deduction for new industry; its domestic_value_added_per_gwh invites use of average VA/GWh, which overstates marginal value. Proposing these fields before r2 computation. Also propose adding WECS (tier 1) and NVVN (tier 5) to the source catalog. Note: units.py already has INR_per_MWh / NPR_per_kWh price codes, which resolves part of 22B's units challenge.

Please deliver the export netback decomposition separately (exchange price, exchange fee, NVVN margin, Indian transmission charges/losses, Nepal-side wheeling) by route and Nepali month, plus import landed cost by month and HP-DAM evening-peak prices; 22E will not re-derive them.

22E needs monthly spill GWh and the months/hours in which the export limit (min of transfer limit and CEA quantum) binds, to classify regimes; monthly averages mask block-level switching between export and import.

Please supply electricity intensity (GWh per NPR of VA) and plausible new electricity-intensive industries with capital cost per unit capacity, so the domestic column is evaluated for industries that could actually locate in Nepal (consistent with 05C RCA flags).

Escalation: if verified, NEA realised export netback below the domestic tariff margin, or import costs above the industrial tariff in dry months, would change strategy conclusions on electricity-led industrialisation (STR proposals) and S05/S09 assumptions; the r2 table must be audited before use.

Red-team note: both the export column (CEA approvals) and the dry-season domestic supply (India-to-Nepal approvals with hour limits) depend on Indian approvals; the domestic-use case is not independent of India in the dry season.

uncertainty: High: nothing retrieved. Structural uncertainties: (i) the sign of the domestic-minus-export difference plausibly changes by regime and season, so any annual average answer is misleading; (ii) average VA/GWh is an upper bound on the domestic column and the marginal value may be much lower once capital and labour opportunity costs are deducted; (iii) export netback depends on approval-limited access and regulated charges that can change discretely; (iv) exchange-price regimes (CERC price caps, 2026 fuel-price conditions) make short price histories unrepresentative; (v) the NPR/INR peg makes INR conversion simple but a peg change is a scenario stress, not a forecast. No probabilities are assigned.

formulas.export_net_value: P_EXP - (C_TRD + C_TX_IN) * FX_INR - C_TX_NP   [if P_EXP is already the NEA border netback, C_TRD and C_TX_IN are already netted and must not be deducted twice]
formulas.domestic_net_value: (VA_IND - K_IND) + T_IND * 1000 - C_GRID, scaled by (1 - LF_DOM) for energy actually delivered   [T_IND converted NPR_per_kWh -> NPR_per_MWh]
formulas.opportunity_cost_of_domestic_use: spill regime: 0; export-marginal regime: export_net_value; import-marginal regime: P_IMP + Nepal-side delivery cost
formulas.net_gain_domestic_minus_alternative: domestic_net_value - opportunity_cost_of_domestic_use (by month, then aggregated to season and Nepal FY with GWh weights)

rows.regime: spill: export limit binding (Q_CAP), surplus beyond limit

export_net_value_NPR_per_MWh.note: marginal export value is zero once the limit binds

binding_caveats: industrial demand must exist in wet season only or tolerate dry-season curtailment
capital idle in dry season unless supplied by imports
approval-limited access: CEA quantum and validity

binding_caveats: import access is itself approval-limited (hour limits)
evening-peak import price (HP-DAM) may exceed industrial tariff: subsidy implied

rows.regime: domestic surplus hours (off-peak / solar hours) with exports
binding_caveats: requires block-level (15-minute/hourly) data, not monthly averages

sensitivities: P_IEX in place of P_EXP (upper bound)
load factor range for demand charges
K_IND with and without new-industry capital
peg-change stress on FX_INR (scenario only, not forecast)
caveats: Demand constraint: domestic value exists only if electricity-intensive industry with plausible comparative advantage (05C RCA table) actually locates in Nepal; average VA/GWh is not marginal VA.

Electricity is one input among many; attributing all of an industry's VA to the GWh overstates the domestic column. The average VA/GWh is an upper bound; the lower bound is the tariff margin over opportunity cost.
Capital cost of new industry (K_IND) and the opportunity cost of that capital and labour must be deducted; otherwise the domestic column ignores resources that would earn returns elsewhere.
Seasonal mismatch: industry needs year-round supply; wet-season surplus value to industry depends on dry-season supply from imports at P_IMP, which may exceed the industrial tariff.
Approval-limited market access: export value exists only for the CEA-approved quantum within its validity; renewal risk is discrete and political (reported 2026 decisions unverified).

Foreign exchange: export earnings are INR (convertible under the peg); domestic industry may earn foreign exchange (exports) or save it (import substitution) - FX effects are reported separately, not added to VA.
Static per-MWh comparison; ignores dynamic effects (learning, employment, fiscal revenue) which are reported under the other welfare objectives, not added here.
